summary: Add Console banner + on-call comms snippet for when hot-route throttling protections are enabled during incidents
description:
Request
- Add a lightweight, incident-safe way for on-call to communicate to internal stakeholders (Support/CS/Sales Eng) when Hot-route capacity protection / priority lanes / throttling protections are actively enabled.
- Provide (1) a Console banner that can be toggled (or auto-driven off protection state) and (2) a copy/paste comms snippet for #support / incident channels.

Why
- During overload events, we’ve seen confusion from internal teams when 429s increase for self-serve traffic while enterprise lanes remain stable. Support needs a consistent explanation, and on-call needs a fast, accurate message.
- Prior incidents/tickets: SUP-24118 (enterprise burst + 429 guidance), SUP-24133 (region inconsistency caused by config propagation delays).

Scope
1) Console banner (internal-facing)
- Audience: internal Redwood users (on-call, Support, CS) viewing Console in incident mode.
- Placement: Console home + relevant throttling dashboard landing page.
- Trigger: manual toggle preferred for v1 (incident commander / on-call); optional auto signal when protection flag enabled in a region.
- Must include: what is enabled, regions affected, expected customer symptoms (429 / Retry-After), link to runbook.
- Must be safe to display during incident (no PII, no customer names, no route names beyond generic “top enterprise routes”).

2) Internal comms snippet
- Provide a standardized message on the ticket that on-call can paste into Slack (#support, #customer-success, and incident channels).
- Include: what changed, what customers may see, what to tell customers (Retry-After + backoff), and where to check status.

Acceptance Criteria
- Banner copy is approved by SRE + Support Readiness.
- On-call can enable/disable banner within 2 minutes (no deploy).
- Banner includes: timestamp, regions, brief reason, and links (runbook + dashboard).
- Comms snippet is stored somewhere stable (Confluence runbook section or Console “Incident notes” panel) and referenced from runbook.

Notes/Constraints
- Do not create customer-visible banners for v1.
- Avoid introducing high-cardinality route info into the banner.
- Keep wording aligned with new standardized 429 semantics (Retry-After, request id, reason codes).

Requested by
- Dev Patel (Support readiness), with input from Owen Phillips (escalations) and SRE on-call rotation.

Primary contacts
- Console: Nora Ahmed / Chloe Martin
- SRE: Rafael Mendes
- Product (semantics): Nikhil Sharma / Lauren Bishop
comments:
2025-01-16 10:12 Dev Patel (reporter): Creating as internal task after SUP-24118 follow-up. Support is getting “why are we throttling me but not them” questions during incidents. We need a consistent internal message + an obvious Console indicator when protections are on.

2025-01-16 11:03 Owen Phillips: +1. During the us-east capacity dip last week, we spent ~20 minutes re-explaining priority lane behavior to CS. Having a banner + a snippet would have reduced back-and-forth.

2025-01-17 09:28 Rafael Mendes (SRE): We can commit to a manual toggle for v1. Auto-driving off config state is nice but not required for launch. Must include a pointer to runbook section “Customer messaging + retry guidance”.

2025-01-17 14:41 Nora Ahmed (assignee): Acknowledged. Proposal:
- Add an internal-only “Incident Notice” banner component in Console admin settings.
- Toggle requires on-call role (existing RBAC group: sre-oncall).
- Fields: Title, body, regions (multi-select), enabled_at, enabled_by.
- v1 will not auto-expire; on-call must disable post-incident.

2025-01-20 13:05 Nikhil Sharma: Copy should not promise “guaranteed” throughput; should say “enterprise priority lanes may be enabled to protect contracted SLOs” and “lower tiers may see increased 429s”. Mention Retry-After compliance.

2025-01-22 16:18 Chloe Martin: Design note: banner will appear on Console landing page and on the “Throttling & Capacity Protection” dashboard link-out page. We’ll also add a “Copy internal comms snippet” button in the banner (copies plain text).

2025-01-27 10:02 Nora Ahmed: Draft banner copy for review:
Title: Capacity protections enabled (priority lanes + throttling)
Body: “To protect platform stability and maintain enterprise route SLOs during elevated load, hot-route capacity protections are currently enabled for selected regions. Some self-serve and non-reserved traffic may receive HTTP 429 responses with Retry-After headers. Advise customers to honor Retry-After and use exponential backoff. See runbook for troubleshooting and customer messaging.”
Links: Overload/Throttling Runbook + Hot-route Protection Dashboards

2025-01-27 10:06 Nora Ahmed: Draft Slack snippet (internal-only):
“FYI: Hot-route capacity protections are ENABLED in {regions} as of {time} to stabilize latency/availability. Expected impact: some self-serve / non-reserved traffic may see elevated 429s (with Retry-After). Guidance: clients should respect Retry-After + exponential backoff; avoid retry storms. Enterprise priority lanes are intended to preserve contracted SLOs. Runbook: {link}. Dashboards: {link}. If you have a customer escalation, share request IDs + region + approximate timestamps.”

2025-01-28 15:22 Dev Patel: Copy looks good. Please add one line explicitly stating: “This is not a billing/quota issue; it’s overload protection.” That’s a common confusion point.

2025-01-29 09:11 Rafael Mendes: Agree w/ Dev. Also add: “If a customer sees 429 without Retry-After, treat as bug and page #eng-oncall.”

2025-01-31 17:48 Nora Ahmed: Implemented changes in Console (internal banner + copy button). Added the two requested lines.
Final banner body includes:
- overload protection vs quota
- Retry-After expectation
- escalation note for missing Retry-After

2025-02-03 12:26 Dev Patel: Verified in prod with SRE test toggle (no customer visibility). Copy button works and message is consistent with Support macros. Marking ready to resolve.

2025-02-04 09:02 Nora Ahmed: Resolved. Follow-up: we should add an auto-expire option (e.g., 6h) to prevent stale banners. Not in scope for this ticket.
